content:
OpenSearch indexes have eventual read consistency. A refresh operation makes all the updates
that are performed on an index available for search. The default refresh interval is one second,
which means that OpenSearch performs a refresh every second while an index is being written to.
The less frequently that you refresh an index (higher refresh interval), the better the overall
indexing performance is. The trade-oﬀ of increasing the refresh interval is that there’s a longer
delay between an index update and when the new data is available for search. Set your refresh
interval as high as you can tolerate to improve overall performance.
We recommend setting the refresh_interval parameter for all of your indexes to 30 seconds or
more.
